English.Char_Desc_2000:
Cellular Automata is a free Conway's Game of Life simulator for Windows from Transys, written by Faiz ul Haque Zeya.
The Game of Life is the best-known cellular automaton. Each cell on a grid is either alive or dead, and in every generation its fate depends only on its eight neighbours: a live cell with two or three live neighbours survives, a dead cell with exactly three live neighbours comes alive, and every other cell dies or stays empty. From these few rules, surprisingly rich patterns emerge.
The program fills a 50 x 50 grid with a random pattern of live cells and plays out the generations on screen. Press Start to run the simulation, pause it at any moment to study the pattern, and press Reset for a fresh random start. It is a simple way to show students or curious friends how complex behaviour grows out of simple rules.
The program is a tiny 75 KB download with no installer: unzip the archive and run Cellular Automata.exe. It requires Windows 10 or 11 with the Microsoft .NET 8 Desktop Runtime, a free download from Microsoft.
Cellular Automata is freeware. There is nothing to buy, no time limit and no registration.
